newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar plant to start cement production in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Qatar plant to start cement production in Nov.

text.p: Qatar National Cement Company said on Monday its second plant will start production in November.
"Construction is almost 85 percent complete and we plan to start production in November 1997," said Mohammed Ali al-Sulaiti, the company's commercial manager.
The plant, being built by France's FCB, a subsidiary of Fives-Lille, at Umm Bab, 85 km (53 miles) west of Doha, would add 2,000 tonnes a day to QNCC's current daily output capacity of 1,500 tonnes.
"God willing, this will make us a net exporter of cement from the end of the year," Sulaiti told reporters.
Qatar has been importing around 1,100 tonnes a day of cement for the past five years to meet rising demand fuelled by a construction boom.
"Our demand has been growing at a rate of 10 to 12 percent annually," he said. He estimated current daily demand at around 2,700 tonnes.
"We hope this figure will go up to around 3,000 tonnes in the coming years as the industrialisation drive gathers further steam," added Sulaiti.
The company hopes to recover the 432 million riyal ($120 million) cost of the new plant from domestic sales and exports within a few years.
QNCC is also exploring possibilities of selling around 500-600 tonnes a day to neighbouring Gulf markets.
"There is enormous building activity in the region and it has potential to take our cement," Sulaiti said.
QNCC is 43 percent owned by the state and the rest by Qatari citizens. Its shares are publicly traded on Qatar's unofficial market.
